about: Every soft site of .github/workflows: why it is soft, when it becomes a gate, and when this declaration lapses. Held to the workflows by scripts/lib/soft_job_gate.py --check (Layer C0); its hosted reading is --hosted-last.

sites.step: multicast on this host, observed (the suites; the leg gates the host witness)
sites.why_soft: observes what the leg cannot gate: the OS's own multicast sends and wz's fuller multicast suites (scouting, pub/sub) run one test at a time; the host witness of multicast is gated in the leg's matrix plane, and these suites flake on Windows (the OS picks among three multicast-capable interfaces) and fail on macOS
sites.gate_when: the suites read green on two consecutive main runs on Windows, and on macOS once they pin an interface the runner lets a spawned process use; until then the macOS row is an observation

observe_only.leg (macos-latest): the suites send on the default interface, which the macOS runner denies to a process it spawns; red on every main run read on 2026-11-21 (six of six), which says nothing about wz

sites.note: the Windows row read green on the six main runs of 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21

sites.step: router interop on this host, observed (one verdict line per question)
sites.why_soft: builds the demo, the host interop tests and a stock router on each host and dials every link; a cold router build is the longest thing the lane does, so the step ends on its own timeout instead of the job, and each verdict line is the reading; tests that earned two green runs are gated by the promoted-tests step after it
sites.gate_when: each link test moves into INTEROP_PROMOTED (scripts/lib/platform_surface_matrix.py) after two consecutive green main runs on its host; the step is a gate once its whole verdict reads green on two consecutive main runs on both hosts
sites.note: read green on both hosts on the six main runs of 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21 (44785492714 to 44869972603): the hosted reading prints promote for it

sites.why_soft: the pico C ABI on the cooperative engine, a second build of the library beside the capi job; every step and the job are observed while the Windows host of the engine is brought up
sites.gate_when: every step of the job is a gate (each after two consecutive green main runs on the Linux and the Windows row); then the job loses continue-on-error
sites.note: the job concluded success on every main run read on 2026-11-21 because its failing steps are soft too; the steps below carry the red

sites.step: the cooperative engine's host and library on this host (observed)
sites.why_soft: the Windows host's unit tests of wz-runtime-posix and the library built on the cooperative engine alone and beside an app transport, each a verdict line
sites.gate_when: two consecutive green main runs on the Linux and the Windows row
sites.note: red on the Windows row on every main run read on 2026-11-21 (six of six, 44785492714 to 44869972603) behind a job that concluded success: the MSVC link of wz-runtime-posix tests and of the wz-capi-pico cdylib leaves the critical-section acquire and release symbols of wz-runtime-coop and wz-session-mcu unresolved (LNK2019); the Linux row is green

sites.step: a single-threaded pico C program on the cooperative engine (observed)
sites.why_soft: a single-threaded pico C program run as a listening and a dialing process on one loopback port, driving its session with zp_read, zp_send_keep_alive and zp_spin_once
sites.gate_when: two consecutive green main runs on the Linux and the Windows row
sites.note: red on the Windows row on every main run read on 2026-11-21 (six of six): the library did not build, for the link failure noted on the step before it

sites.step: the cooperative engine's teardown over tcp (observed)
sites.why_soft: two cooperative-engine peers over tcp on the loopback exchange round trips, then each teardown call of the dialling one must return in time with its peer open and with its peer gone; a new program on both hosts, observed as each new program of this job starts
sites.gate_when: two consecutive green main runs on the Linux and the Windows row, each with its verdict line reading 2 passed
sites.note: added on 2026-11-22 with no main run read yet

sites.step: a single-threaded pico C program on the library without std (observed)
sites.why_soft: the single-threaded pico C program of the step before it, run against the library built without std (os-posix on Linux, os-windows on Windows, the capi-nostd profile) in a target directory of its own; a new form of the library on both hosts
sites.gate_when: two consecutive green main runs on the Linux and the Windows row
sites.note: added on 2026-11-22 with no main run read yet

sites.why_soft: the packaging dry-run of zenoh-pico-sys on a release tag is informational: a non-zero exit becomes a warning so the release artefacts still land, because the wz-codecs build script runs codegen from vendor/sce and the source tree exceeds the crates.io tarball cap until an exclude list prunes it
sites.gate_when: the dry-run passes on a release run once the package exclude lists land; then the step drops its || echo and a packaging error fails the release
sites.note: release.yml runs on a v* tag, never on a main push, so --hosted-last reads no run of it; read a release run with --hosted <run-id>
